name: VS Code, GitHub & developer tools
description: Visual Studio Code, GitHub and GitHub Copilot, Visual Studio and Microsoft developer platforms.

items.title: Visual Studio 2026 version 18.11.3 addresses security advisories
items.summary: Microsoft released Visual Studio 2026 version 18.11.3 on October 29 with security advisory fixes. The listed issues include a libcurl HTTP/2 upload use-after-free, a Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write, and a Visual Studio certificate-validation vulnerability.

items.title: GitHub adds webhook delivery IP ranges to the Meta API
items.summary: GitHub added three webhook delivery IP ranges to the Meta API’s `hooks` field. Operators maintaining static allowlists should add the prefixes to avoid rejecting deliveries; the change applies across GitHub.com plans, including Enterprise Cloud.

items.title: Microsoft details vcpkg’s October update, including configurable cache compression
items.summary: Microsoft summarized October changes to vcpkg, including a configurable binary-cache compression level, improved cache diagnostics and reliability, and updated ports such as Boost 1.92.0. The compression option lets developers trade ZIP archive size against cache submission time.

items.title: Microsoft and Syncfusion collaborate on open-source Blazor toolkit and contributions
items.summary: Microsoft announced a collaboration with Syncfusion to advance Blazor. Syncfusion has released a free, MIT-licensed component toolkit and contributed fixes and tests to ASP.NET Core and .NET scaffolding, adding reusable components while contributing directly to the platform.

items.title: Microsoft Copilot harness enters public preview in Foundry Agent Service
items.summary: Microsoft introduced the Copilot harness in Foundry Agent Service as a public preview, giving developers a managed way to build agents that reason, use tools, and complete complex, long-running tasks. The post also announced general availability of long-running resilience for hosted agents.

items.title: Visual Studio Marketplace adds secretless Trusted Publishing for extensions
items.summary: Microsoft announced Trusted Publishing for Visual Studio Marketplace extensions. GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines can use verified federated identity to publish without storing a long-lived personal access token or publishing secret; existing PAT-based publishing remains available.

items.title: Microsoft makes Copilot UX components generally available with SPFx 1.24
items.summary: Microsoft made Copilot UX components generally available worldwide with SharePoint Framework 1.24, allowing developers to bring interactive dashboards, forms, and business actions into Copilot conversations. Components can also be reused in SharePoint, Teams, and Outlook; users need a Microsoft Copilot add-on license to render them in Copilot.

items.title: Copilot code review adds Max effort preview and generally available approvals
items.summary: GitHub added a Max effort level for Copilot code review in public preview and made Copilot approvals generally available. The combination is intended to provide a deeper review and an approval assessment within the pull-request review workflow.

items.title: Visual Studio Code 1.144 stable release expands agent workflows and continuity
items.summary: VS Code 1.144 shipped in the stable channel with expanded agent workflows, including agent sessions that continue across environments and client continuity supported by the Agent Host Protocol. The release also brings agent management and model-selection updates, making it a substantial IDE update for developers using Copilot agents.

items.title: GitHub brings Copilot Agent Merge into cloud pull requests
items.summary: GitHub integrated Agent Merge into pull requests on GitHub.com. Copilot can watch for blockers such as failing Actions workflows and merge conflicts and attempt to fix them; the cloud feature is available to paid Copilot users subject to organization and enterprise policies.

items.title: GitHub Copilot Fusion reaches general availability for model routing
items.summary: Copilot Fusion is now generally available, letting users delegate model selection and orchestration to Copilot instead of choosing a model for each task. It is available across all Copilot plans in VS Code, the GitHub Copilot app, Copilot CLI, and JetBrains IDEs, with Standard, High, and Max effort levels.

items.title: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105 fixes Fusion effort selection in long-context sessions
items.summary: Copilot CLI 1.0.105 fixes an issue that prevented users from selecting Copilot Fusion High or Max from /model during long-context sessions. The official release page records publication on October 28.

items.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows reaches general availability
items.summary: GitHub Agentic Workflows is generally available on GitHub.com for Free, Team, and Enterprise. It lets users define reasoning-based automations in Markdown for compilation into GitHub Actions workflows, with GA additions including self-hosted runner support, improved budget forecasting, model routing, and stronger agent isolation.

items.title: Copilot Fusion previews intelligent routing between local and cloud models
items.summary: Copilot Fusion’s experimental preview can route requests between supported on-device and cloud models in Copilot CLI, the Copilot app, and VS Code. The announcement includes managed Windows setup for MAI Code 1.1 Flash and support for manually configured local models; it notes that routing still makes decisions in the cloud.

items.title: GitHub Copilot app adds Projects and computer use in public preview
items.summary: The GitHub Copilot app introduced Projects in public preview, providing a home for work spanning repositories and sessions. It also announced computer use in public preview on macOS and Windows, allowing Copilot to interact with desktop applications, including apps without APIs or MCP integrations.

items.title: GitHub Enterprise begins including access to Copilot for licensed users
items.summary: GitHub Enterprise customers working with a GitHub or Microsoft account team can now include Copilot access for each licensed user, with AI-credit budgeting applying to some capabilities. This changes how eligible enterprises manage Copilot access, while self-serve subscriptions remain unaffected and will receive availability in stages.

items.title: GitHub Copilot previews natural-language image generation and editing
items.summary: Copilot users can now generate and edit images with natural-language instructions without leaving Copilot. The feature is in public preview for Pro, Pro+, Business, and Enterprise plans, with image-token usage billed separately and counted against plan AI credits.

items.title: GitHub rolls out shared Copilot Automations for teams
items.summary: Shared Copilot Automations let teams build and maintain AI-powered workflows together in repositories. Automations are visible to repository readers, editable by those with write access, and billed to the repository owner; GitHub says rollout is underway for Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise plans.

items.title: GitHub introduces intelligence features for Copilot memory, context, and code search
items.summary: GitHub announced a context and learning layer for agents, including Copilot Memory, now generally available on paid plans, and Copilot dreaming, in public preview. Memory can carry personal preferences and repository conventions across sessions and clients, while dreaming reviews prior work to improve future agent sessions.

items.title: GitHub previews a Security extension for the Copilot app
items.summary: GitHub introduced a public-preview Security extension in the Copilot app that surfaces repository code-scanning alerts and lets users ask Copilot to explain or help fix them. The preview is available on github.com and GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency; Enterprise Server is not supported.

items.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows introduces a pre-run admission gate
items.summary: GitHub Agentic Workflows now documents an opt-in admission gate that can consult a separately deployed authority before an agent session starts. The authority can approve or deny activation and return AI-credit allowances, enabling centralized policy and budgeting; the post emphasizes this is cooperative, not a hard quota.

items.title: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.104 changes Auto model selection and Autopilot task waiting
items.summary: Copilot CLI 1.0.104 changes managed fusion sessions to start on Auto and apply fusionTier settings. Interactive and SDK Autopilot sessions now continue waiting for attached background tasks instead of stopping at the configured timeout; `-p --autopilot` still honors that timeout.

items.title: VS Code adds configurable eagerness for GitHub Copilot inline suggestions
items.summary: VS Code now lets paid GitHub Copilot subscribers choose low, medium, or high eagerness for inline suggestions. The settings let developers tune how proactively Copilot offers suggestions and how large its proposed edits are.

items.title: GitHub Copilot assisted permissions reach general availability
items.summary: GitHub made Copilot assisted permissions generally available in Copilot CLI, the Copilot app, and VS Code. The mode automatically proceeds with requests judged clearly safe and requires user approval for other requests; enterprise administrators can manage access to the mode.

items.title: GPT-6.1 Terra becomes generally available in GitHub Copilot
items.summary: GPT-6.1 Terra is now generally available in GitHub Copilot for Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise users, with rollout across VS Code, Visual Studio, CLI, the cloud agent, and other clients. GitHub positions it for everyday agentic coding and terminal work at a lower cost than GPT-6.1 Sol; usage-based billing follows provider list pricing.

items.title: Visual Studio adds resumable, unsaved Markdown investigation notes
items.summary: Visual Studio 2026 version 18.11 can create standalone Markdown notes, and the opt-in Hot Exit preview can restore unsaved notes after Visual Studio is closed and reopened. This helps developers resume investigations without having to save the note or add it to a project first.

items.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows weekly update highlights hardening and safer credential handling
items.summary: GitHub Agentic Workflows’ October 26 weekly update recaps six hardening releases, emphasizing stronger static analysis, safer credential handling, and clearer diagnostics. Highlighted changes include network credentials for safe-output integration jobs and secret-safe error diagnostics for engine-driver crashes.
